Hi Perry,

Thank you for your response. Here is my code:

# Calculate Initial Constants
mu_lam1 <- mean(data$count, na.rm = TRUE)
nyear <- length(unique(data$year))
ndelta <- length(unique(data$Variable))
nscale <- length(unique(data$Scale))
nsite <- length(unique(data$site))
nvisit <- max(data$visit)

# Initialize count array
count_array <- array(NA, dim = c(nvisit, nyear, ndelta, nscale, nsite))

# Populate count_array with counts
for (i in 1:nvisit) {
  for (j in 1:nyear) {
    for (k in 1:ndelta) {
      for (s in 1:nscale) {
        for (v in 1:nsite) {
          subset_data <- data %>%
            filter(visit == unique(data$visit)[i],
                   year == unique(data$year)[j],
                   Variable == unique(data$Variable)[k],
                   Scale == unique(data$Scale)[s],
                   site == unique(data$site)[v])

          count_array[i, j, k, s, v] <- if (nrow(subset_data) > 0) {
            mean(subset_data$count, na.rm = TRUE)
          } else {
            NA
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Initialize detection covariates Array
X_det <- array(NA, dim = c(nvisit, nyear, ndelta, nscale, nsite))

for (v in 1:nvisit) {
  for (t in 1:nyear) {
    for (d in 1:ndelta) {
      for (s in 1:nscale) {
        for (i in 1:nsite) {
          subset_values <- data %>%
            filter(year == unique(data$year)[t],
                   Variable == unique(data$Variable)[d],
                   Scale == unique(data$Scale)[s],
                   visit == unique(data$visit)[v],
                   site == unique(data$site)[i]) %>%
            pull(Value)

          X_det[v, t, d, s, i] <- if (length(subset_values) > 0) {
            mean(subset_values, na.rm = TRUE)
          } else {
            NA
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
# Display results
list(mu_lam1 = mu_lam1, nyear = nyear, nvisit = nvisit, ndelta = ndelta, nscale = nscale, count_array = count_array, X_det = X_det)

# Define the NIMBLE Model
nimblemodel <- nimbleCode({
  ### Priors
  off <- 0.00001
  ss ~ dunif(1, (nscale - off))
  ss_trunc <- trunc(ss)
  prop_scales <- ss - ss_trunc

  for (i in 1:nsite) {
    for (t in 1:nyear) {
      # Linear interpolation for cover variables
      w_tree_height[i, t] <- tree_height[i, t, ss_trunc] * (1 - prop_scales) +
        tree_height[i, t, ss_trunc + 1] * prop_scales
      w_canopy_cover[i, t] <- canopy_cover[i, t, ss_trunc] * (1 - prop_scales) +
        canopy_cover[i, t, ss_trunc + 1] * prop_scales
      w_grassland[i, t] <- grassland[i, t, ss_trunc] * (1 - prop_scales) +
        grassland[i, t, ss_trunc + 1] * prop_scales
      w_forest[i, t] <- forest[i, t, ss_trunc] * (1 - prop_scales) +
        forest[i, t, ss_trunc + 1] * prop_scales
    }
  }

  # Initial year
  alpha0 ~ dnorm(mu_lam1, sd = 2)
  sd_alpha ~ dunif(0, 5)

  # Fixed effects
  beta0 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1)
  beta_tree_height ~ dnorm(0, sd = 3)
  beta_canopy_cover ~ dnorm(0, sd = 3)
  beta_grassland ~ dnorm(0, sd = 3)
  beta_forest ~ dnorm(0, sd = 3)

  # Detection
  delta[1] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 2)
  delta[2] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 2)
  for (j in 3:ndelta) {
    delta[j] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 3)
  }
  sd_p ~ dunif(0, 5)

  ### Likelihood
  # Latent process
  for (i in 1:nsite) {
    llam[i] ~ dnorm(alpha0, sd = sd_alpha)
    log(lam[i, 1]) <- llam[i]
    N[i, 1] ~ dpois(lam[i, 1])

    for (t in 1:nyear) {
      lam[i, t] <- N[i, t] * exp(
        beta0 +
          beta_tree_height * w_tree_height[i, t] +
          beta_canopy_cover * w_canopy_cover[i, t] +
          beta_grassland * w_grassland[i, t] +
          beta_forest * w_forest[i, t]
      )
      N[i, t] ~ dpois(lam[i, t])
    }
  }

  # Observation process
  for (j in 1:nvisit) {
    mu_l_p[j] <- inprod(delta[1:ndelta], X_det[j, 1:ndelta])
    l_p[j] ~ dnorm(mu_l_p[j], sd = sd_p)
    logit(p[j]) <- l_p[j]

    # Using unique identifiers for the observations
    y_j <- count_array[year_id[j], , , site_id[j], visit_id[j]]
    y[j] ~ dbin(p[j], sum(y_j, na.rm = TRUE))

    # Compute fit statistic
    eval[j] <- p[j] * sum(y_j, na.rm = TRUE)
    y_new[j] ~ dbin(p[j], sum(y_j, na.rm = TRUE))
    E[j] <- pow((y[j] - eval[j]), 2) / (eval[j] + 0.5)
    E_new[j] <- pow((y_new[j] - eval[j]), 2) / (eval[j] + 0.5)
  }
  fit <- sum(E[1:nvisit])
  fit_new <- sum(E_new[1:nvisit])
  bpvalue <- step(fit - fit_new)

})

# Parameters to Monitor
params <- c("alpha0", "sd_alpha", "beta0", "sd_p", "delta")

# Define initial values for the parameters
init <- list(
  beta = c(0, 0),
  ss = 1,
  alpha0 = 0,
  sd_alpha = 1,
  sd_p = 1,
  delta = rep(0, ndelta)
)

# Prepare data for NIMBLE
nimble_data <- list(
  y = data$count,  # Your response variable
  year_id = as.integer(factor(data$year)),
  site_id = as.integer(factor(data$site)),
  visit_id = as.integer(factor(data$visit)),
  count_array = count_array,
  X_det = X_det,
  nsite = nsite,
  nyear = nyear,
  nvisit = nvisit,
  ndelta = ndelta,
  nscale = nscale
)

# Compile the Model
compiled_model <- nimbleModel(nimblemodel, data = nimble_data, inits = init)

Hey Frank,

My commentary may or may not be helpful here so take it with a grain of salt. Does X_det vary in all 5 dimensions? If so, I think you would want your observation (mu_l_p) to also be able to vary across sites, years, etc. Right now you only have it set up as varying with visit.

Instead of:

mu_l_p[j] <- inprod(delta[1:ndelta], X_det[j, 1:ndelta])

I would do:

for (v in 1:nvisit) {
  for (t in 1:nyear) {
    for (d in 1:ndelta) {
      for (s in 1:nscale) {
        for (i in 1:nsite) {

           mu_l_p[v,t,d,s,i] <- inprod(delta[1:delta], X_det[v,t,1:delta, s, i])
         l_p[v,t,d,s,i] ~ dnorm(mu_l_p[v,t,d,s,i], sd = sd_p)
    logit(p[v,t,d,s,i]) <- l_p[v,t,d,s,i]

and then adjust your y-variable accordingly.

-Heather

Thanks Heather for contributing on this. Frank, let me suggest how we can get to the bottom of this. In a case like this, we are mostly going to look at your code in terms of software mechanics rather than statistical meaning (but sometimes that), so that is what I am trying to follow. When you had X_det set up as five dimensional and used it as two dimensional, it was hard for me to guess what you were trying to do. Now you have tried using X_det as five dimensional in the model and you reported that it's still not working, so we will need to see that to try to figure out what is going on. What really can work well is if you can reduce the context of the problem by cutting away parts of the model are not related (i.e. remove as much as you can so it is as simple as possible to demonstrate the problem) and providing a completely reproducible example (meaning that we can run your code and reproduce the error you are seeing). Often a good way to do that is to provide code to simulate relevant data, and that is easier to do once you have removed parts of your model that are not relevant to the problem. So if you can make such a minimal reproducible example and send it, then people on the list can run your code and make suggestions.
Fingers crossed we can get things sorted out for you.
Perry

messages.body_plain:
Hi Perry and Heather,

Thank you all for dislodging me from the headache that I have been going through for longer now. Usually, I like working on my code and analysis for all possible avenues until I feel I got to the dead end then I would reach out for assistance. I have been trying this code for a while now and everything seems right till this part, model compilation "# Compile NIMBLE Model
nimble_model <- nimbleModel(code = nimblemodel,
                            constants = list(mu_lam1 = mu_lam1,

                                             nsite = nsite,
                                             nyear = nyear,
                                             nvisit = nvisit,
                                             ndelta = ndelta,

                                             nscale = nscale),
                            data = list(count_array = count_array))
". I appreciate taking a look at my code and hopefully it might work. I have attached both my recent most code and the data that I'm using. Ideally, I have 24 species of my interest (A,B,C....), counted in 24 sites during three visits in three years to form dependent variable. I also have four environmental variable that I would like to use as predictor using their values and understand what scale is best explaining. The scales are 250m,500,1000 and 2000m.
Please let me know if this information is sufficient to understand my objective with the NIMBLE code, and if not, I would more than will to provide additional information.

##Code
#  Libraries
library(coda)
library(nimble)
library(posterior)
library(tidyverse)
##Call in the data

# Calculate Initial Constants
mu_lam1 <- mean(data$count, na.rm = TRUE)
nyear <- length(unique(data$year))
ndelta <- length(unique(data$Variable))
nscale <- length(unique(data$Scale))
nsite <- length(unique(data$site))
nvisit <- max(data$visit)

# Initialize count Array

count_array <- array(NA, dim = c(nvisit, nyear, ndelta, nscale, nsite))

# Populate count_array with counts per year-variable-scale-site-visit combination

for (i in 1:nvisit) {
  for (j in 1:nyear) {
    for (k in 1:ndelta) {
      for (s in 1:nscale) {

        for (v in 1:nsite) {  # Loop for visits

          subset_data <- data %>%
            filter(visit == unique(data$visit)[i],
                   year == unique(data$year)[j],
                   Variable == unique(data$Variable)[k],
                   Scale == unique(data$Scale)[s],

                   site == unique(data$site)[v])  # Filter by visit as well

          # Calculate the mean of count if data exists, otherwise assign NA

          count_array[i, j, k, s, v] <- if (nrow(subset_data) > 0) {
            mean(subset_data$count, na.rm = TRUE)
          } else {
            NA
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

print(dim(count_array))

# Initialize detection covariates array: Dimensions (Visit, Year, Variable, Scale, Site)

X_det <- array(NA, dim = c(nvisit, nyear, ndelta, nscale, nsite))

# Populate X_det for each combination of visit, year, variable, scale, and site

for (v in 1:nvisit) {
  for (t in 1:nyear) {
    for (d in 1:ndelta) {
      for (s in 1:nscale) {

        for (i in 1:nsite) {  # Include site dimension

          subset_values <- data %>%
            filter(year == unique(data$year)[t],
                   Variable == unique(data$Variable)[d],
                   Scale == unique(data$Scale)[s],
                   visit == unique(data$visit)[v],

                   site == unique(data$site)[i]) %>%  # Filter by site as well

            pull(Value)

          X_det[v, t, d, s, i] <- if (length(subset_values) > 0) {
            mean(subset_values, na.rm = TRUE)
          } else {
            NA
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Define dimensions based on unique values
n_sites <- length(unique(data$site))
n_years <- length(unique(data$year))
n_visits <- length(unique(data$visit))
n_scales <- length(unique(data$Scale))

# Initialize arrays for each variable type with appropriate dimensions
tree_height_array <- array(NA, dim = c(n_sites, n_years, n_visits, n_scales))
canopy_cover_array <- array(NA, dim = c(n_sites, n_years, n_visits, n_scales))
grass_cover_array <- array(NA, dim = c(n_sites, n_years, n_visits, n_scales))
forest_cover_array <- array(NA, dim = c(n_sites, n_years, n_visits, n_scales))

# Populate variable arrays for each combination of site, year, visit, and scale
for (i in 1:n_sites) {
  for (t in 1:n_years) {
    for (v in 1:n_visits) {
      for (s in 1:n_scales) {
        # Filter data for tree height
        tree_height_values <- data %>%
          filter(site == unique(data$site)[i],
                 year == unique(data$year)[t],

                 visit == unique(data$visit)[v],

                 Scale == unique(data$Scale)[s],

                 Variable == "Tree Height") %>%
          pull(Value)

        # Assign mean value if available
        tree_height_array[i, t, v, s] <- if (length(tree_height_values) > 0) {
          mean(tree_height_values, na.rm = TRUE)
        } else {
          NA
        }

        # Filter data for canopy cover
        canopy_cover_values <- data %>%
          filter(site == unique(data$site)[i],
                 year == unique(data$year)[t],

                 visit == unique(data$visit)[v],

                 Scale == unique(data$Scale)[s],

                 Variable == "Canopy Cover") %>%
          pull(Value)

        # Assign mean value if available
        canopy_cover_array[i, t, v, s] <- if (length(canopy_cover_values) > 0) {
          mean(canopy_cover_values, na.rm = TRUE)
        } else {
          NA
        }

        # Filter data for grass cover
        grass_cover_values <- data %>%
          filter(site == unique(data$site)[i],
                 year == unique(data$year)[t],

                 visit == unique(data$visit)[v],

                 Scale == unique(data$Scale)[s],

                 Variable == "Grass Cover") %>%
          pull(Value)

        # Assign mean value if available
        grass_cover_array[i, t, v, s] <- if (length(grass_cover_values) > 0) {
          mean(grass_cover_values, na.rm = TRUE)
        } else {
          NA
        }

        # Filter data for forest cover
        forest_cover_values <- data %>%
          filter(site == unique(data$site)[i],
                 year == unique(data$year)[t],

                 visit == unique(data$visit)[v],

                 Scale == unique(data$Scale)[s],

                 Variable == "Forest Cover") %>%
          pull(Value)

        # Assign mean value if available
        forest_cover_array[i, t, v, s] <- if (length(forest_cover_values) > 0) {
          mean(forest_cover_values, na.rm = TRUE)
        } else {
          NA
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Define the NIMBLE Model
nimblemodel <- nimbleCode({
  ### Priors
  off <- 0.00001
  ss ~ dunif(1, (nscale - off))
  ss_trunc <- trunc(ss)
  prop_scales <- ss - ss_trunc

  for (i in 1:nsite) {
    for (t in 1:nyear) {
      # Linear interpolation for cover variables

      w_tree_height[i, t] <- tree_height_array[i, t, ss_trunc] * (1 - prop_scales) +
        tree_height_array[i, t, ss_trunc + 1] * prop_scales
      w_canopy_cover[i, t] <- canopy_cover_array[i, t, ss_trunc] * (1 - prop_scales) +
        canopy_cover_array[i, t, ss_trunc + 1] * prop_scales
      w_grassland[i, t] <- grass_cover_array[i, t, ss_trunc] * (1 - prop_scales) +
        grass_cover_array[i, t, ss_trunc + 1] * prop_scales
      w_forest[i, t] <- forest_cover_array[i, t, ss_trunc] * (1 - prop_scales) +
        forest_cover_array[i, t, ss_trunc + 1] * prop_scales

    }
  }

  # Initial year
  alpha0 ~ dnorm(mu_lam1, sd = 2)
  sd_alpha ~ dunif(0, 5)

  # Fixed effects
  beta0 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1)

  for (i in 1:nsite) {
    for (t in 1:nyear) {

      for (j in 1:ndelta) {
        # Define beta for each variable
        beta[i, t, j] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1)
      }
    }
  }

  # Likelihood

  for (i in 1:nsite) {
    for (t in 1:nyear) {

      for (v in 1:nvisit) {

        count_array[v, t, , ss_trunc, i] ~ dpois(lambda[v, t, i])
        lambda[v, t, i] <- exp(alpha0 + beta[i, t, 1] * w_tree_height[i, t] +
                                 beta[i, t, 2] * w_canopy_cover[i, t] +
                                 beta[i, t, 3] * w_grassland[i, t] +
                                 beta[i, t, 4] * w_forest[i, t])
      }
    }
  }
})

# Compile NIMBLE Model
nimble_model <- nimbleModel(code = nimblemodel,
                            constants = list(mu_lam1 = mu_lam1,

messages.body_plain:
Hi Etienne,

A follow-up on this. I mis-diagnosed the problem in the original setting. It's not the `dcat` statements, but rather that the result of the stochastic indexing is a vector rather than a scalar. Our AD system doesn't support that. We'll make some changes to the system to error trap this and give an informative error message.

There's some discussion of the issue in this GitHub issue <https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/issues/1500>.

A work-around is that if you do want to use AD with your model, you could do the stochastic indexing one-by-one, like this:

gammaTmp[i,j,1:2] <- c(gamma[z[i,j-1],1] gamma[z[i,j-1],2])
z[i,j] ~ dcat(gammaTmp[i,j,1:2])
omegaTmp[i,j, 1:2] <- c(omega[z[i,j],1], omega[z[i,j],2])
y[i,j] ~ dcat(omegaTmp[i,j,1:2])

Or if the vector was long, you could have a loop instead of using `c`, illustrated here only for `gammaTmp`:
for(k in 1:K)
   gammaTmp[i,j,k] <- gamma[z[i,j-1],k]

You might also be able to make use of the discrete hidden Markov model distributions in the nimbleEcology package.

-chris
